You are an evaluator for a speculative-futures simulation. You will read a
documented starting world, a set of stipulated drivers, and a candidate world
two years later. You score it on three independent axes. You are rigorous,
literal and unimpressed by drama. You hold the candidate to the drivers and the
starting state: a change with no mechanism is a flaw, a magnitude out of range
for two years is a flaw, and spectacle is not severity.

messages.content: {"least_plausible_claims":[{"quote":"The country is medicated on weekdays and comes off the drug on weekends.","field":"prose/closing_paragraph","why":"Mechanism: semaglutide and the oral products have long half-lives, so skipping a weekend has no pharmacological effect. The world's own holidays are defined as 2–6 weeks, and the prose has Dr. Patel saying 'a day or two won't matter with the pill'. The weekend-spike economy (bars, NFL handle, QSR, 'off-weekend' tasting nights) therefore rests on a mechanism the world contradicts."},{"quote":"About 12.5 million Medicare beneficiaries obtain incretins through the new obesity route in its first year; Part D plans require pills before injections","field":"world/events/3/event","why":"Magnitude and mechanism: 12.5M new users in the first 12 months, behind prior authorisation and step therapy, is a very fast ramp. It is tied to a rule that overrides a statutory exclusion, and the candidate shows no uptake chain such as prescriber capacity, PA throughput or plan behaviour."},{"quote":"the company files to extend the label to obese adults without heart disease, with no FDA decision expected before 2037","field":"world/events/1/event","why":"Mechanism: this event dates the filing to 2035-06, but pipeline_note says Lilly filed the sNDA in Feb 2036. The two disagree by eight months, and a standard review from the earlier date would produce a decision well before 2037."}],"badness":{"flourishing":5.5,"autonomy":6.0,"inequality":5.5,"public_health":5.5,"cohesion":6.0,"epistemic":4.5,"overall":5.8},"plausibility_axes":{"driver_fidelity":8.5,"mechanism":5.5,"magnitude":8.0},"generativity":8.0,"rationale":{"badness":"Starting from the 2026 baseline, the world inherits employer adherence premiums, a 15% gray market, counterfeit-product harms, childhood growth deficits and about 98M users. It adds an anhedonia label (6.8% vs 3.1%), a projected ~9,000 excess hip fractures a year by 2038, and a muscle-and-bone class gap among unscanned Medicare and Medicaid oral users. Broader access (Medicaid, Part D, obesity down to 30.3%) and a nameable, labelled harm soften it, so epistemic scores lowest, but hidden low-dose exposure in ~19M lean users and the ADA/adherence tension keep it a recognisably harder society, about a 6.","plausibility":"driver_fidelity: every driver is visibly realised. The CMS rule and Medicaid/Part D mandates give public_expansion, the 2035 label gives anhedonia_labelled, prices fall $299→$279 and $219→$199, no approvals occur, and the personality layer is a mainstream complaint. Class stratification is shown through DXA and muscle markers. mechanism: the weekend-holiday economy contradicts the world's own 2–6 week holiday definition and the long-half-life pharmacology (claim 1), and the Lilly filing date differs between events and pipeline_note (claim 3). Several shifts are also asserted rather than shown, such as 'Thinness no longer signals class' despite 30% obesity and the first-year Medicare ramp (claim 2). magnitude: 35.5% on-drug and 45% ever-used sit inside the envelope, and the payer mix sums to 98.0M. The age and income checks, Part D ($62.8B) and Medicaid ($16.8B) arithmetic, and the cash breakdown all reconcile. Minor flaws: the pediatric count is slightly under 1.3%, and 12.5M first-year new users is an aggressive ramp.","generativity":"The prose follows Rosalind through a day: the 5:40 pill, Medicaid copay, her patient Mr. Delacroix with the thinning arms, a Memphis cousin's vial photo, her ten-year-old son and the legal wait until twelve, and the weekend-off question. The porch beer and the street cheering without her close it. The world fields add many scenes (off-weekend nights, holiday codes, Columbus arms and gait, Bread Alone potlucks), though some are explained rather than shown."}}

messages.content: {"least_plausible_claims":[{"quote":"Of the ≈36.1M off now, about 9M are on a bone pause or stopped after a DEXA result","field":"world/population/note","why":"Fails mechanism and magnitude. A 90-day pause that applies only at T ≤ −2.5 and only when no antiresorptive is co-prescribed cannot leave 9M people off at one time. The world itself describes an antiresorptive co-prescribing boom, and 9M off at a time implies a flow of roughly 36M pauses a year."},{"quote":"two rival filers say the 100% tariff on their Indian-made sterile product makes launch uneconomic anyway","field":"world/access/generic_rest_of_world","why":"Fails mechanism. Indian generic semaglutide sells for $5–30/month, while US cash prices are $299–379 and public rates $199. A 100% tariff on declared value would leave a large margin, so the stated reason for not launching does not follow."},{"quote":"≈10% monthly MariTide (≈11M, about 5.5M publicly paid, many pharmacy-administered)","field":"world/access/note","why":"Fails magnitude and mechanism. MariTide was a top-third product at $549 in 2034 and reached Part D only in Sep 2035. About 11M users within roughly 15 months, from a single manufacturer's supply and pharmacy shot-day infrastructure, is asserted with no ramp shown."}],"badness":{"flourishing":6.0,"autonomy":6.5,"inequality":6.0,"public_health":6.5,"cohesion":5.5,"epistemic":5.0,"overall":6.5},"plausibility_axes":{"driver_fidelity":8.5,"mechanism":6.5,"magnitude":7.5},"generativity":8.0,"rationale":{"badness":"About 39% of adults are on the drug, with ≈26,000 excess hip fractures a year, ≈3,000 NAION cases, ≈840k excess anhedonia cases if causal, 1.3M children on drug, and ≈10.9M gray-market users. Autonomy loss is structural: tenure gates on ≈40% of gated plans, kiosk-weight premiums, employers steering low-wage staff to Medicaid, mandatory bone pauses, and monthly shots that log adherence and remove the dose holiday. Against 2026 this is a clearly harder society with new losers, but harms are named and measured and Medicaid access has widened, so it stays below 7.","plausibility":"driver_fidelity: All ten drivers are visible in fields and events: shock_up through the tariff and price rise, public expansion through the 2035 law, pediatric 6–11 approval, the bone wave, MariTide as an existing product in new forms, eleven restriction states, and the grey as a mainstream complaint. The approval timings fit the envelope rules. mechanism: Most chains are shown, but the 9M bone-pause stock and the claim that the tariff makes generic launch uneconomic (claims 1 and 2) are asserted without a working chain. magnitude: Current use (39.0%), ever use (52.0%), income thirds, age bands (sum 108.4M) and payer mix (sum 108.4M) all reconcile, and the Medicare and Medicaid spending arithmetic checks out. Minor gaps remain: the ≈$205 blended net is below the ≈$220 implied by the stated payer prices, the 3% hip-fracture rate rise sits oddly against an ≈8% excess, and the 11M MariTide ramp (claim 3) is aggressive.","generativity":"The prose gives a concrete character in Lorraine Pruitt, with specific places (Huber Heights, the Kroger on Wilmington Pike), a DEXA reading of −2.3, the Telegram lot lists, and the Tammy and Kaylee subplots.
